outputs.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: realistic 3D Unity space game asteroid concept art, shared art-direction comparison board, first concept iteration.
Create a refined landscape concept sheet with three equally sized vertical columns against flat near-black charcoal. Minimal understated white German typography. Exact title: "ASTEROIDEN · STILSTUDIE 01". Column titles exactly: "EISREICH", "FELSIG", "METALLREICH". Each column contains one large detailed isolated asteroid in the upper two-thirds, with plenty of margin, entirely visible without cropping, no overlap. Below each large asteroid show one SMALL distant-view rendering of THE SAME asteroid at approximately 64-pixel visual width with broad material cues still readable, then three small square surface texture samples. Exact short lower-row label: "FERNANSICHT". Main objects have comparable apparent size; this sheet compares composition, not physical scale. No arbitrary numbers or scientific claims.
Common style: convincing high-end photorealistic physically based 3D space rendering, observational planetary geology, restrained natural desaturated palette. One common neutral-white directional sunlight from upper left, stark cast shadows with only very subtle neutral bounce/fill for presentation; no atmospheric fog, no blue studio rim light. Main visual structure is irregular low-frequency large masses, secondary cliffs/crater basins/fractures, then fine regolith detail. No spheres, no smooth potatoes, no repetitive noise-coated mesh, no Earth landscape pasted on a sphere.
LEFT / ICE-RICH: deeply dark charcoal carbonaceous rock and dust crust covering approximately 90-95 percent of visible surface; asymmetrical partially bilobate chunky body with a broad eroded neck, terraces, pits and broken crust. Only 2-3 localized uneven exposed water-ice patches inside recessed fractured scarps, cool off-white to faint gray-blue, matte granular ice, patches big enough to remain visible as a few light shapes in the distance thumbnail. Crust edges partially obscure the ice. Never a blue crystal, snowball or transparent iceberg. No glowing ice, no pervasive frost.
CENTER / ROCKY: an angular elongated but compact asymmetric broken silicate mass, warm gray and muted taupe, matte fractured coherent bedrock with broad planar fracture faces, rubble pockets, one large impact cavity and layered broken ledges. Clearly different silhouette from left and right. No exaggerated orange saturation, no visible ice, no colorful gemstones.
RIGHT / METAL-RICH: compact asymmetrical squat wedge, battered and pitted, muted graphite and iron-nickel gray with a few broad rough exposed metallic regions partially covered by dark regolith and silicate inclusions. Restrained broad specular reflections on large worn facets establish a material distinction at thumbnail size. Mostly dusty and rough, never a polished chrome object or molten ore; tiny muted bronze-gray touches allowed but no Earth-like pervasive orange rust. No crystal spikes, no machinery.
The distance thumbnails must show the exact same large-body design above them, identical lighting and corresponding surface patches, credible reduced-detail appearance. Surface samples reflect each design. No ships, no logos, no watermarks, no stars, no planets, no bloom, no UI beyond requested typography. This is a GAME ART DIRECTION, not a claim that composition can be reliably inferred from a real asteroid's shape.

Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: second realistic 3D Unity asteroid concept sheet, morphological variant exploration.
Input image 1 is a STYLE AND MATERIAL REFERENCE ONLY, not an edit target. Create a NEW landscape concept sheet with nine DISTINCT asteroid concepts in an orderly 3 by 3 grid, using the exact visual language and realistic material rendering of reference image 1. Each asteroid entirely visible in its own cell, clear separation, understated editorial white typography on near-black charcoal.
Exact title: "ASTEROIDEN · FORMVARIANTEN 02". Column headers left to right: "EISREICH", "FELSIG", "METALLREICH". Row labels: "100 m", "1 km", "5 km". Exact footer: "Ansichten auf gleiche Bildgröße normiert · keine Maßstabsdarstellung". Physical size labels denote approximate maximum body extent. IMPORTANT: show all nine at approximately equal apparent size in their grid cells to study morphology; never pretend that the 100 m object and 5 km object share an actual scale. Each successive row is a newly designed specimen, not just a scaled clone.
Common art direction: photoreal physically based observational geology in space. Neutral white sun from upper-left, common light across all specimens, dark shadows, very subtle neutral presentation fill, no atmosphere, no colorful rims. Low-frequency readable silhouettes and broad surface regions dominate; moderate detail, not uniform tiny noise. Irregular non-spherical forms at all sizes. Family forms are deliberate game visual cues and allowed to vary without implying a scientific shape classification.
Ice-rich left column: ALL objects must be overwhelmingly dark charcoal dusty rocky crust, approximately 90-95% covered, only two or three local off-white matte exposed ice patches at fractured cliffs or recessed depressions, 5-10% of visible area at most. Subtle cool gray, no bright cyan, no glow, no giant ice crystals or snow coating. 100 m: short asymmetric fractured dark nugget with a deep notch and one or two pale ice windows. 1 km: elongated bilobate contact-like body with broad neck, broken crust, distinct few pale ice windows. 5 km: irregular multi-lobed eroded mass, broad dark dust plains and steep broken scarps, a few localized exposed pale ice recesses.
Rocky middle column: warm gray/taupe matte dry silicate, coherent jagged planar fracture faces, natural regolith pockets, no metallic gleam or ice. 100 m: angular broken elongated shard, visually chunky rather than crystal-thin. 1 km: oblique asymmetric block mass with one large broken crater. 5 km: squat asymmetric elongated basin-bearing body, large impact depression, broad scarps, rubble patches, still not spherical.
Metal-rich right column: muted graphite to iron-nickel gray, irregular compact forms, battered pits and low-frequency broad rough exposed metallic facets partly veiled by dark dust/regolith and silicate inclusions. Moderately broad restrained metallic reflections, NOT shiny chrome, not molten, no gold ore veins, no pervasive terrestrial orange rust. 100 m: dense rough squat irregular wedge with one exposed worn reflecting facet. 1 km: compact asymmetric pitted knuckle shape with a large broad metallic scar. 5 km: large squat asymmetrical faceted lump with crater depression and fragmented dark regolith mantles.
Make family differences readable through silhouette plus broad material appearance, retaining shared visual realism. Distinct silhouettes for each of the nine. No ships or drones, no scale bars, no extra labels, no icons, no stars, no planets, no watermarks, no bloom.
